answer: Vesting delays blunt sybil farms: every reward an identity earns stays locked for, say, 30 epochs, and any slashing event during that window claws back the whole unvested pile. A swarm of fake agents built like a sand dune looks solid until one gale of fraud detection hits; then every linked account loses months of income at once. Honest agents keep a long-lived stake as their anchor, so waiting costs them little, while an attacker must fund thousands of identities for weeks before cashing out anything.
